name: manual_56dd36
claim: A single review-fix brief covering two PRs across two repos can silently misattribute a finding's file to the wrong PR -- verify each finding's file path actually exists in the PR/repo it's filed under before starting work on it, don't assume the brief's grouping is correct

decisions.notes: The orama-321.md brief bundled findings from BOTH orama-system PR #321 (review #4983422918) and Perpetua-Tools PR #359 (review #4989313231) under what read as one continuous numbered list. Two items -- orchestrator/tiered_pipeline.py's trace_id-before-path-resolution finding, and .agent/memory/candidates/graduated/a045e9f02292.json's version-qualify finding -- were listed under the orama-321 heading but the files don't exist anywhere in orama-system's history; both actually belonged to the PT-359 review. Caught by grepping for the file in orama-system BEFORE starting to fix it there, not after. Fixing an orama-system-side finding for a file that only exists in PT would have either silently failed (file not found) or, worse, prompted creating a stray file in the wrong repo to 'satisfy' the finding.
